To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed an active ester-functional polypyrrole that can be conjugated with NGF, and that NGF immobilization on the active ester polypyrrole film does not affect the electroconductivity and neurotrophic activity of NGF.
we developed a new method of conjugating nerve growth factor (a neuroactive molecule) to a conductive polymer (poly(pyrrole)) without impairing the conductivity of the polymer.
the copolymer PPy-NSE was synthesized and used as a platform for immobilizing nerve growth factor (a neurotrophic factor) on the copolymer surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel electroconductive scaffolds that are able to provide neurotrophic activity and are stable for long-term cell culture.
the synthesis and characterization of electroconductive polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) scaffolds with active ester groups, which can be modified with nerve growth factor.
the development of a novel electroconductive polymer that can be used as an active scaffold for nerve tissue engineering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a novel scaffold that is electrically conductive and bioactive.
we have developed a novel and efficient method for immobilization of neuroactive molecules on conductive polymer surfaces.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel method to conjugate NGF onto the electroconductive polymer surface, and this conjugated NGF can be used for neuronal cell culture and differentiation.
we have successfully prepared an electroconductive and stable NGF-immobilizing scaffold for neuronal tissue engineering and biosensing.

this study has demonstrated that the copolymerable PPy-NSE is an effective and stable platform for immobilizing NGF, which retains good conductivity and neurotrophic activity for PC12 cell differentiation and neurite extension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the active ester groups can be introduced to polypyrrole films and used to immobilize NGF without significantly hindering conductivity or stability of the scaffold.

we have developed a new strategy for immobilizing bioactive molecules on electroconductive scaffolds without significantly compromising the conductivity of the scaffold and the bioactivity of the ligands.

the incorporation of neurotrophic ligands into electroconductive scaffolds via a specific and robust approach can be achieved without significantly compromising the electroconductive and biological properties of the scaffolds.
